Read an .xlsx or CSV file and say what importing it would do: the rows
ready to import, likely duplicates, and the problems keeping rows out.
Saves nothing.

Import the ready rows of the same file the preview read, in one
transaction, creating the categories they name that don't exist yet.

Rows with problems are left out. So are likely duplicates, unless
`include_duplicates` is true.

schema.title: Response List Budgets Api V1 Finance Budgets Get

get.description:
The budgets that apply to a month, with spend measured against each cap.

A monthly budget is measured over that month alone; a custom one over its
whole range, in every month it touches. Separate from GET /budgets rather
than folded into it: this one converts currencies, and the forms that only
need the list of budgets should not pay for an exchange-rate lookup.

schema.title: Response List Currencies Api V1 Finance Currencies Get

get.description: Spent, budgeted and remaining for a date range, in the display currency.

Spend per category over a date range, in the display currency.

Both filter parameters are optional and default to everything. `category_ids`
absent means every category, including any created since the caller last
looked; `include_uncategorized` switches off the bucket holding spend whose
category was deleted, which has no id to name it by.

Spend per day or per calendar week over a range, in the display currency.

The bar chart picks the granularity from how long the range is, so that a
week shows seven bars and a quarter shows thirteen rather than ninety.

Both filter parameters are optional and default to everything. `category_ids`
absent means every category, including any created since the caller last
looked; `include_uncategorized` switches off the bucket holding spend whose
category was deleted, which has no id to name it by.

BillingInterval.title: BillingInterval
BillingInterval.description: Unit of a subscription's billing cycle; paired with an interval count.

BucketSpendRead.title: BucketSpendRead
BucketSpendRead.description:
One bar: what a single day or week cost.

The range is inclusive and, for weeks, can be shorter than seven days where
the bucket is clipped by the ends of the window — label the bar with it
rather than assuming every bar covers the same span.

BudgetPeriod.title: BudgetPeriod
BudgetPeriod.description: How a budget's window is measured.

BudgetProgressRead.title: BudgetProgressRead
BudgetProgressRead.description:
A budget with what has been spent against it.

``currency`` is the budget own currency rather than the display currency:
spending is converted *into* the cap so the percentage means something
fixed. Two budgets in a list may therefore be quoted in different currencies.

CategorySpendRead.title: CategorySpendRead
CategorySpendRead.description: One slice: what a single category cost over the range.

ExpenseExportRequest.title: ExpenseExportRequest
ExpenseExportRequest.description:
What the Transactions tab is showing: its rows by id, its filters in words.

Ids rather than filters because the tab filters in the browser; sending
the result keeps the filtering in one place. The cap is decades of daily
spending, and exists so one request cannot ask for an unbounded IN list.

ExpenseImportPreviewRead.title: ExpenseImportPreviewRead
ExpenseImportPreviewRead.description: What importing a file would do. Nothing has been saved.

ImportProblemRead.title: ImportProblemRead
ImportProblemRead.description: Why one cell keeps its row out of the import.

ImportRowRead.title: ImportRowRead
ImportRowRead.description: One expense a file would import, as the importer read it.

ListOrderUpdate.title: ListOrderUpdate
ListOrderUpdate.description:
A list's new order, as the ids of the rows on screen, first to last.

May name only part of the list — the Budgets tab shows one month's
budgets — in which case those rows swap among the places they already
hold and the rest stay put. The cap is far past any one person's list and
exists so a request cannot ask for an unbounded IN list.

NotificationUpdate.title: NotificationUpdate
NotificationUpdate.description:
Exactly one action: mark read or unread, snooze or unsnooze a reminder,
or move a notice to the history.

ProfileUpdate.title: ProfileUpdate
ProfileUpdate.description:
All-optional: apply with model_dump(exclude_unset=True).

Only display_name may be sent as null (or blank), which clears it.

SummaryRead.title: SummaryRead
SummaryRead.description:
Totals for a date range, expressed in the profile's display currency.

Expenses and budgets keep whatever currency they were recorded in; only
these totals are converted, and at today's rates — so a figure for last
month can move as rates move. That is the documented trade-off in
app.services.exchange_rates, not a bug.
